sections.h2: What DeepSeek V4.1 Flash actually costs in October 2026
paras: $0.15 per 1M input and $0.60 per 1M output are off-peak rates. DeepSeek bills double during two weekday windows, 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC, which cover seven hours a day, five days a week — about 21% of the calendar. Weekends and Chinese public holidays bill off-peak all day, so roughly 79% of the week sits at the rates on this page.

Cache hits cost $0.003 per 1M tokens, fifty times cheaper than a miss at $0.15. For an agent that resends the same system prompt most of the input never pays the full rate: the worked example below runs at $2.33 a month instead of $6.30.

The 1017 snapshot, released 2026-10-17, kept the price and cut output length by roughly 30%. Cost per finished task fell without a rate change, which is why per-token price is a poor proxy for cost per outcome.

sections.h2: V4.1 Flash or V4 Pro: when the cheap tier is enough
paras: Flash is 4.4x cheaper on input and 3.3x cheaper on output than V4 Pro, and it wins on two things besides price: it accepts images, which Pro rejects, and it allows 2,500 concurrent requests against Pro's 500. For extraction, classification, vision and high-volume fan-out there is no reason to pay the premium.

Where Pro earns its price is long-horizon reasoning. If a wrong answer costs more than the tokens, the cheaper model is the expensive choice — the 3.7x gap on the cached loop above is worth paying when a retry chain costs an hour of engineering time.

faq.q: How much does DeepSeek V4.1 Flash cost per 1M tokens?
faq.a: $0.15 per 1M input tokens and $0.60 per 1M output tokens at off-peak rates. Weekday peak (01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC) doubles both, to $0.30 and $1.20. Cached input bills at $0.003 per 1M.

faq.q: Is DeepSeek V4.1 Flash cheaper at night?
faq.a: Yes. Off-peak rates are half the peak rates. Peak covers seven hours per weekday, so about 79% of the week bills at the lower rate; weekends and Chinese public holidays are off-peak all day.

faq.q: Should I use V4.1 Flash or V4 Pro?
faq.a: Flash for extraction, classification, image input and high-concurrency work: it is 4.4x cheaper on input and 3.3x cheaper on output, accepts images, and allows 2,500 concurrent requests against 500. Use V4 Pro when reasoning depth is worth the premium.

faq.q: Does DeepSeek V4.1 Flash accept image input?
faq.a: Yes. Flash is multimodal while V4 Pro is text-only, which is often the deciding difference for document, screenshot and chart workloads.

Same price, but outputs run about 30% shorter, so cost per completed task dropped. The model name is deepseek-flash; the retired deepseek-v4-flash aliases are served by this snapshot and billed at the Flash price.

sections.h2: What DeepSeek V4 Pro actually costs in October 2026
paras: $0.66 per 1M tokens is the off-peak rate, not the list price. DeepSeek publishes peak rates and halves them outside two weekday windows: 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC. That is seven hours a day, five days a week, about 21% of the calendar. The other 79% bills at the rates above, and Chinese public holidays count as off-peak all day.

Cache hits are the widest lever here. A cache hit costs $0.022 per 1M tokens against $0.66 for a miss, a 30x difference. An agent that resends the same long system prompt pays full price for it once and almost nothing afterwards, which is why the worked example below drops from $25.74 to $8.51 a month.

There is no batch-API discount for this model. DeepSeek does not publish one, so the 50% asynchronous saving that OpenAI, Anthropic and Google offer has no equivalent here. Time-of-day pricing replaces it, and it is worth the same 50% if your jobs can wait for an off-peak window.

sections.h2: V4 Pro or V4.1 Flash: what the price gap buys
paras: V4 Pro costs 4.4x more on input and 3.3x more on output than V4.1 Flash. Two non-price differences decide the call: V4 Pro is text-only while Flash accepts images, and V4 Pro's concurrency limit is 500 against Flash's 2,500, which matters when you fan out hundreds of parallel requests.

Route by task shape rather than by model rank. Extraction, classification, image input and short chat belong on Flash; long-horizon reasoning where a wrong answer is expensive justifies Pro. Sending every request to Pro at 4.4x the input rate is rarely the right default.

sections.h2: The hidden cost: Search and Fetch billing starts 1 November 2026
paras: DeepSeek bills its Search and Fetch APIs per request at $0.75 per 1,000 successful calls, and those calls are free until 00:00 Beijing time on 1 November 2026. From that date retrieval becomes a separate line item, so a search-heavy agent pays twice: once for tokens and once for lookups.

Worked example: five search calls per turn, 20 turns a day, is 3,000 calls a month, or $2.25. That is about 26% on top of the $8.51 token bill above. For retrieval-heavy workloads the search line can exceed inference, and no token calculator will show it.

faq.q: How much does DeepSeek V4 Pro cost per 1M tokens?
faq.a: $0.66 per 1M input tokens and $1.98 per 1M output tokens at off-peak rates. Weekday peak (01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC) doubles both, to $1.32 and $3.96. Cached input bills at $0.022 per 1M.

faq.q: Is DeepSeek V4 Pro cheaper at night?
faq.a: Yes. Off-peak rates are half the peak rates. Peak covers seven hours per weekday, so about 79% of the week bills at the lower rate; weekends and Chinese public holidays are off-peak all day.

faq.q: Does DeepSeek V4 Pro have a batch API discount?
faq.a: No. DeepSeek does not publish a batch discount for this model, so the 50% asynchronous saving offered by OpenAI, Anthropic and Google has no equivalent here. Off-peak pricing and cache hits are the available levers.

faq.q: Should I use V4 Pro or V4.1 Flash?
faq.a: Flash for extraction, classification, image input and high-concurrency fan-out: it is 4.4x cheaper on input and 3.3x cheaper on output, accepts images, and allows 2,500 concurrent requests against 500. Use V4 Pro when reasoning depth is worth the premium.

faq.q: What does DeepSeek charge for Search and Fetch?
faq.a: $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests, free until 00:00 Beijing time on 1 November 2026. After that, retrieval is billed separately from tokens and can add around 26% to a search-heavy agent's bill.
